questions.question: For prophylactic immunization of poliomyelitis OPV used is:

options.A: Salk + sabin vaccine given by injection

questions.explanation: Oral polio vaccine (OPV) is the Sabin live attenuated vaccine given by mouth.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Medicine/Davidson/20th Ed./Pg. 138-139

questions.question: There are a variety of different isolation categories which require the use of specific techniques designed to reduce or prevent the transmission of disease. Which of the following is required regardless of the specific isolation category?
questions.explanation: Handwashing is required in every category of isolation precaution.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 68/

questions.question: A physical therapy program designs study that uses performance on the scholastic aptitude test as a prediction of grade point average in a physical therapy academic program. The results of the study identify that the overall correlation between the variables is r=.87. Which statement is most accurate based on the results of the study?

options.A: Grade point average in a physical therapy program is a function of performance on the scholastic aptitude test
options.B: A student that performs well on the scholastic aptitude test is likely to have a high grade point average in a physical therapy academic program
options.C: There is no relationship between grade point average in a physical therapy program and performance on the scholastic aptitude test
options.D: There is an inverse relationship between grade point average in a physical therapy program and performance on the scholastic aptitude test

questions.explanation: A strong positive correlation (r = 0.87) means high scorers on one variable tend to score high on the other; it does not prove causation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methodology for Clinical Therapists/ Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 101

questions.question: A therapist designs a research study which examines the effect of functional knee bracing on speed and agility. In this study speed and agility are the:
questions.explanation: The outcome measured (speed and agility) is the dependent variable; bracing is the independent variable.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapist/ Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 70

questions.question: A group of physical therapy students develops a physical activity survey as part of a community health screening. The survey consists of a series of question in which subjects must respond year or no. This type of survey utilizes a/an ___ level of measurement?
questions.explanation: Yes/no responses form a nominal scale.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 34

questions.question: A therapist measures the vertical leap of members of a basketball team. The therapist then calculates the difference between the highest and lowest values in the distribution. What measure of variability has the therapist determined?
questions.explanation: Range is the difference between the highest and lowest values.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 54

questions.question: A group of senior physical therapy students utilizes ten patients from a local rehabilitation center with decubitus ulcers for a research project. This type of sampling most accurately describes:
questions.explanation: Using ten readily available patients is convenience (non-probability) sampling.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 27

questions.question: A therapist compares the significance of the mean vertical leap difference between samples of 12 athletes and 10 nonathletes. How many degree of freedom are there in study?
questions.explanation: For two independent groups df = n1 + n2 - 2 = 12 + 10 - 2 = 20.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 119

questions.question: A group of physical therapy students present a research project entitled "Effects of Ultrasound on Blood Flow and Nerve Conduction Velocity." The dependent variable in the student' study is:

options.D: Blood flow and nerve conduction velocity

questions.explanation: Blood flow and nerve conduction velocity are the outcomes (dependent variables); ultrasound is the independent variable.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 32

questions.question: A therapist participates in a study which examines knee range of motion at selected postoperative intervals. After collecting the necessary data, the therapist prepares to measure the spread or dispersion of the range of motion at each interval. Which statistical measure would be the most appropriate to meet he therapist's objective:
questions.explanation: Variance (and standard deviation) measures spread; median, mode and mean are central tendency measures.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 55

questions.question: What percentage of physical therapy students taking their state board examination would you expect to score within plus and minus one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.explanation: About 68 percent of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 49

questions.question: A therapist is asked to indicate on a five point scale how competent a patient is in a selected transfer technique. The scale ranges from totally incompetent to extremely competent. The type of scale utilizes a/an _______ level of measurement?
questions.explanation: A rating scale from incompetent to competent is ordinal.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 35

questions.question: The middle score of a distribution which divides a group of scores into equal parts with half of the scores falling above and half of the scores falling below describes the:
questions.explanation: The median is the middle score that divides a distribution into two equal halves.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 50

questions.question: A group of therapists conduct a research study which examines the effect of functional keen bracing on speed and agility. As part of the study the therapists determine measures of central tendency for each measured test. Which of the following would not be considered a measure of central tendency?
questions.explanation: Range is a measure of dispersion, not central tendency.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/5th Ed./Pg. 55

questions.question: A physical therapy department plans a study to examine rehabilitation outcomes in patients who have undergone anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction. The study will include a sample of patients from 25 orthopedic surgeons in the local region. If the therapists compile a list of all eligible patients and select every third patient to participate in the study, what type of sampling was used?
questions.explanation: Choosing every nth subject from a list is systematic sampling.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 27

questions.question: A therapist conducts a study which measures knee flexion range of motion two weeks following arthroscopic surgery. Assuring a normal distribution what percentage of patients participating in the study would you expect to achieve a goniometeric measurement value greater than one standard deviation below the mean:
questions.explanation: Values above one SD below the mean comprise 50 + 34 = about 84 percent.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 49

questions.question: A therapist presents the results of a research project entitled "Effect of an Aerobic Exercise Program on Heart Rate and Blood Pressure." The independent variable in the therapist's study is:

options.D: Heart rate and blood pressure Assessment and Examination

questions.explanation: The exercise programme is the independent variable; heart rate and blood pressure are the dependent variables.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/Pg. 32

questions.question: When two therapists give drastically different manual muscle testing results on the same patient, it is an example of poor:
questions.explanation: Differing results between two different testers is poor interrater reliability.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Research Methods for Clinical Therapists/Hicks/4th Ed./Pg. 77l

questions.question: A 20-year-old women rehabilitating from a head injury is unable to bathe and dress herself independently. This would correctly be identified as a/an:
questions.explanation: Inability to perform activities such as bathing and dressing is a disability (activity limitation).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 8/

questions.question: A therapist uses patient care gloves to prevent the transmission of infection. When is it appropriate to reuse patient care gloves?

options.A: When the gloves are used to treat same patient
options.B: When the gloves are used by the same therapist
options.C: When the gloves do not come in contact with any potentially infections material

questions.explanation: Disposable patient-care gloves must not be reused; change them between tasks and patients and wash hands.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 12

questions.question: as per the WHO's ICIDH classification impairment means:

options.A: Pathological processes due to microbes attacking a human body
options.B: Inability to perform activities of daily living with physiological dysfunction
options.C: Disabled, ambulatory on wheelchair with psychological impairment
options.D: Any loss or abnormality of psychological, physiological or anatomical structure or function

questions.explanation: In the WHO ICIDH, impairment is any loss or abnormality of psychological, physiological or anatomical structure or function.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 1337

questions.question: A therapist visits a former patient diagnosed with pneumonic plague in the hospital. The patient is in strict isolation, but the therapist has been granted permission to visit if there is no body contact. What protective measures are necessary when entering the room of a patient in strict isolation?
questions.explanation: Strict isolation requires mask, gown and gloves.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 19

questions.question: A ramp which begins at ground level and ends 18 inches above ground should be at least ________ feet long?
questions.explanation: For a 1:12 gradient an 18-inch rise needs an 18-foot ramp.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation/Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 409

questions.question: In rehydration therapy ORS used is:
questions.explanation: ORS stands for oral rehydration solution.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential Pediatrics/O.P. Ghai/6th Ed./Pg. 272

questions.question: Which statement concerning the APGAR newborn assessment is not true?

options.A: The test is administered at 1 and 5 minutes after birth
options.C: A score of less than 4 is indicative of respiratory distress
options.D: The score for each assessed item range from 0-2

questions.explanation: The maximum Apgar score is 10, not 5.

questions.question: A therapist treats a 15-year-old female of Spanish descent. The patient speaks only a few words of English and has significant difficulty understanding the therapist's instructions. The most appropriate therapist action is to:

options.A: Speak strongly and directly to the patient
options.B: Encourage frequent feedback from the patient

questions.explanation: An interpreter should be used when there is a language barrier.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Mean + 1.96 SD covers ___________.
questions.explanation: Mean plus or minus 1.96 SD covers 95 percent of a normal distribution.

questions.question: The most common measure of variability is _________.
